samples.xml_description:
<module id="sequence_detector">
    <description>Design a sequence detector to detect the binary sequence 1001.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="reset_n">Asynchronous active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in">Binary input signal representing the incoming bitstream.</input>
        <output id="sequence_detected">Output signal indicating whether the sequence has been successfully detected.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">Waiting for the start of the sequence.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">The first bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">The second bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">The third bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S4">The fourth and final bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" type="state">Current state of the sequence detector.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" type="state">Next state of the sequence detector.</reg>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n)>
            if (~reset_n)
                current_state <= IDLE;
            else
                current_state <= next_state;
        </always>
        
        <always @(*) begin
            case(current_state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1)
                        next_state = S1;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S1: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0)
                        next_state = S2;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S2: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0)
                        next_state = S3;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S3: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1)
                        next_state = S4;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S4: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1)
                        next_state = S1;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                default: next_state = IDLE;
            endcase
        end
        
        <assign sequence_detected = (current_state == S4 && data_in == 1'b1)? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>The sequence detector detects the binary sequence 1001 using a sequential logic approach. It consists of four states: IDLE, S1, S2, and S3, representing the different stages of detecting the sequence. The state machine transitions between states based on the input data_in and the current state. The output sequence_detected is asserted when the sequence is completely detected.</implementation>
</module>
